transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of Search, ZephyrSearch), Tom Baxter (CTO), Ibrahim Khan (Sr ML Eng)

Summary: Redwood walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for ZephyrSearch relevance use case. Demo covers embedding API, search pipeline using kNN + reranker, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (SSO/KMS/SOC2), and proposed pilot steps.

Topics: embeddings dims & indexing, rerank models, API examples, batching & caching, security & data residency, benchmarking plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Carlos from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Lena: Good, thanks. Excited to see how you handle reranking, we've had issues with our current ranking pipeline.
[00:09] Tom: Hi all, quick background — we run multi-tenant search across docs and product data, latency needs to be under 120ms p95 at query time, and costs have been creeping up.
[00:15] Carlos: Great, thanks for that context Tom. We'll walk through a hosted API demo that shows embeddings for vector search, then the rerank endpoint that re-scores a small candidate set to improve relevance without blowing up latency.
[00:22] Ibrahim: Quick Q up front — do you do hybrid search (BM25 + vectors)? We currently combine Elastic with vector neighbors.
[00:26] Carlos: Yep, hybrid is common. We typically do an initial candidate generation (BM25 or ANN) and then call Redwood's rerank to re-score top-K. The hosted embeddings endpoint can also be used for dense-only pipelines.
[00:34] Maya: We'll demo both flows — first a dense-only with kNN, then hybrid + rerank. Carlos, can you share your screen?
[00:39] Carlos: Sharing. Alright, starting with the API playground. Here's the embeddings endpoint example — POST /v1/embeddings with a short snippet, returns a 1536-d vector by default for our recommended open model.
[00:47] [00:47] Carlos: Note — model choice affects dim and cost, we surface that in the console and API. We'll switch to a smaller dim model for demo to keep latency low.
[00:55] Carlos: Here's a sample code snippet in Node — call embeddings, upsert to a vector index (we show integration with popular vector stores, and we also provide an integrated managed index).
[01:03] Lena: When you say managed index, is that Pinecone-like? Are you hosting it?
[01:06] Carlos: Managed index is Redwood-hosted optimized storage with approximate search. It's similar to Pinecone for get-started convenience, but with integrated optimizations for our runtime. For customers with strict controls you can bring-your-own index or use Dedicated/Private.
[01:15] Ibrahim: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? We see repeated queries and want to cache cold-start costs.
[01:20] Carlos: For embeddings/ rerank, caching comes at two layers: prefix/KV on the token stream for generation models, and result caching at the query level for embeddings/rerank. We recommend TTL on frequent queries and automatic cache invalidation on doc updates.
[01:28] [02:00] Carlos: Now the rerank endpoint — POST /v1/rerank where you pass the query and candidate set (top K ids + snippets). The endpoint runs a small cross-encoder re-scoring model and returns scores and reordered ids. Here's a live example with 10 candidates.
[02:09] [02:09] Ibrahim: Latency? If we do cross-encoder on top-10, what's typical p95?
[02:13] Carlos: For our hosted profile, cross-encoder on top-10 with our small rerank model is typically 40-120ms depending on sequence length and load. We give SLOs and you can opt for a faster distilled rerank model to hit lower p95 at expense of some accuracy.
[02:22] Tom: That sounds in range. What's the cost per query vs running a bigger model?
[02:26] Maya: Pricing is per-call for rerank + per-embedding for vectorization. We'll send a cost example sheet after the call — it depends on candidate K, token lengths for snippets, and model class.
[02:33] [03:10] Carlos: Demo note — here's a rerank pipeline we set up earlier for Zephyr sample data. We show before/after metrics: MRR improved by ~12% and click-through simulated improvements. Caveat: this is synthetic sample, results will vary on your corpus.
[03:22] Lena: Nice. Can you show how this looks in the Console? We want to see traces and cost breakdown per route.
[03:27] Carlos: Sure — switching to Console. On the left is model catalog, the middle has per-route dashboards. You can see token-level cost, latency percentile, and error rates. We also have a trace view that surfaces which step (embedding call, index fetch, rerank) dominated latency.
[03:37] [04:00] Carlos: For rollouts, the Console supports canary and A/B routing — run rerank variant A vs B on a percentage of traffic and compare top-line metrics. Also built-in evals let you tie prompt sets to regression alerts.
[04:09] Ibrahim: Security — we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and keys in our KMS. How does hosted handle KMS?
[04:14] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via integration with major cloud KMS providers for data-at-rest encryption. We also provide detailed audit logs and can enable SSO/SAML for enterprise accounts. For stricter requirements, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option.
[04:22] Tom: Data residency — some data must stay in EU. Is host region control available?
[04:25] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported for hosted; we can ensure inference and storage remain in EU regions. For regulated workloads we often recommend Private.
[04:31] [05:00] Carlos: Back to the demo — quick look at sample latency distribution and cost per 1k queries in the Console report. I want to highlight batching: if you batch embeddings upsert you'll dramatically lower per-vector cost, but that implies some ingestion latency. For query-side rerank batching is less common since you need near-instant responses.
[05:13] Ibrahim: For our search traffic, queries are usually single-shot low latency. We can batch during offline indexing though.
[05:17] Carlos: Exactly — most customers do batched ingestion for embeddings and single-shot rerank at query time.
[05:22] [07:00] Carlos: Now a short live run — I'll call the embeddings endpoint for a sample product snippet, insert into the managed index, then call /search which does ANN then /rerank.
[07:08] [07:08] Carlos: (typing) — sending embedding, upsert ok, running search, returning top-10, calling rerank, final results returned in ~95ms.
[07:15] Lena: That looks good; how stable under load? We need predictable p95 at scale.
[07:20] Carlos: We surface dedicated capacity options — Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with capacity guarantees and configurable autoscaling. That path removes noisy neighbor concerns.
[07:27] Tom: If we go dedicated, can we still use the Console?
[07:29] Maya: Yes — same Console UX across hosted, dedicated, and private. You can pin models and rollout policies per environment.
[07:34] Ibrahim: For our POC, we want to run a benchmark with our dataset and compare to our Elastic+current reranker. Can you run that for us?
[07:38] Maya: Yes, Carlos will run a benchmark on a 1-hour window sample if you can provide a data dump or an S3 link.
[07:41] Carlos: I'll need a representative set of queries and documents and a small evaluation script — we can reuse your labels if you have them, otherwise we'll do simulated click evals.
[07:48] Tom: I'll put together an S3 link and share by Tuesday.
[07:52] [10:00] Carlos: Quick note on model selection — we recommend smaller embedding dims for large corpora (e.g., 512–768) for cost savings, larger dims (1536) may give quality boost for nuanced semantics. For rerank, small cross-encoder models are good balance. We also support quantized model variants in Dedicated to lower GPU costs.
[10:20] Lena: Any integration examples with our frontend? We use a Go backend and React search UI.
[10:25] Carlos: We have SDKs and example snippets — Node/Python/Go. For search UI you simply hit your backend which orchestrates embed + index + rerank calls; SDKs handle retries and backoff.
[10:32] [15:00] Maya: Let's cover common objections — latency vs cost: you can reduce cost by using cheaper embedding models or reducing K, and reduce latency by using distilled reranker or moving to Dedicated. For security/regulatory we offer VPC/on-prem options.
[15:12] Tom: We also care about observability for regressions — do you keep historical evals?
[15:16] Carlos: Yes, Redwood Optimize stores eval runs, can alert on regression tied to a prompt set or metric like MRR/precision@k. You can configure thresholds and automatic rollbacks.
[15:25] Ibrahim: Are there any limits on candidate text length for rerank?
[15:28] Carlos: The rerank model has token limits similar to typical transformer models — we recommend truncating long docs to most relevant snippet. Long sequences increase latency.
[15:35] [30:00] Maya: Quick recap and proposed pilot: 3-week POC where Redwood runs embeddings + rerank benchmark on your dataset, show before/after relevance metrics and cost estimates. Deliverables: benchmark results, Console access to a demo project, and security docs.
[30:12] Lena: Sounds good. What's the expected cost for a pilot?
[30:15] Maya: We'll provide a pilot pricing sheet; typically pilots are low-cost or credit-backed, depending on whether you need dedicated capacity for the run.
[30:22] Tom: Please include requirements for dataset format and expected IAM/credentials.
[30:26] Maya: Will do.
[30:30] [40:00] Carlos: Final notes — common pitfalls: using too large K for candidate gen, not truncating context for rerank, and not batching ingestion. We'll include best-practices doc in the follow-up.
[40:12] Ibrahim: Thanks, this was helpful and pretty concrete.
[40:15] Lena: Agree, next steps look clear.
[40:18] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll send the pricing & security pack and propose pilot dates.
[40:25] Tom: Thanks all.

Recap / Next steps (as read out in call):
- Maya to send pricing, SSO/SOC2 summary, and best-practices doc by 2028-03-08.
